# Scout A: gate notes (2026-11-19)

Candidates: 2946 (with lead 2947), 2950, 2945, 2554. Rows are in `scout-A.tsv`. Images are in
`sources/cache/cross/<id>/` (gitignored). The ASF IIIF server gives at most 1272 to 1352 px (from `info.json`).

**Measuring.** `line/sign_height.py` crashed on the raw ASF JPEGs. The server writes a "Generated by iipsrv"
comment into the file, `magick` copies it into the PGM header as a `#` line, and the header parser does not
skip `#` lines. I measured on copies made with `magick <jpg> -strip <png>` and left the script unchanged.
The script needs a comment-skipping fix before anyone measures ASF images with it.

## 2946 / 2947: Gonzaga to Cosimo, 1439. Fails Readable (11 px); strongest otherwise
- c. 215 (image 432) is one page with about 14 lines of cipher mixed with clear Italian. It is dated "Ex Sablo die
  xxiiij Januarij 1439" and signed "Johannesfranciscus Marchio Mantue". The clear text names "el Magnifico Conte
  Aluise" and "Francesco da Landriano". Nothing is written between the lines.
- Lead 2947 is filza XI **viewer images 691-694**, not cc. 691-694; filza XI ends before image 1378. Image 691 is
  dated "31 Xbre 1439" in a later hand, 694 ends "Ex [Sermide?] die ultimo decembris 1439" with the Marquis's
  signature, and 690 is the address leaf, to Cosimo. All of 691, 692, 693 and 694 carry a **contemporary
  interlinear word-by-word decipherment** in a second hand. It is the same sign set as c. 215: H, delta, psi, pi,
  the ladder signs, "-o-", and digit groups such as 19, 32 and 68. By eye that is about 4000 glossed signs,
  which makes it the largest pair in this set. 695 is a clear letter of 3 Jan 1440 by another writer.
- Measured: 11 px on c. 215, 10 px on 691 and 11 px on 692. That is no. 1336's figure, where readers agreed at
  0.80.
- **What would change the verdict:** if the cross-section accepts 1336-level images and works by readers' votes
  (METHOD step 3), 2946 passes every other gate easily. The pair is enormous and the target is short and bare.
- URLs: https://archiviodistatofirenze.cultura.gov.it/iipsrv/iipsrv.fcgi?IIIF=/data/iip-data/asfi/mediceo_avanti_principato/00100011/A0000432.ptif/full/full/0/default.jpg
  and the same path with A0000691 to A0000694.

## 2950: Guidantonio da Montefeltro to Cosimo, [1438]. Fails Readable (13 px)
- A small landscape leaf with short runs of a digit-and-letter cipher (o, 9/q, 4, 8, 3, x, k) inside clear
  Italian, about 300 signs in all. It has stains on the left and nothing written between the lines.
- Even with a lower floor this item has no pair. It would depend on the BAV Urb. lat. 998 keys (DECODE R212,
  1440-69) fitting, and I did not test them.

## 2945: Francesco Sforza to Cosimo, Lodi 1454. Fails Readable (13 px)
- c. 201 holds about 60 lines of cipher, about 2000 signs. The signs are well formed, dark and separated,
  readable by eye, and include numerals 12-29 and 55-56 that are probably codes. c. 202 has more cipher among
  Italian. Nothing is written between the lines.
- **What would change the verdict:** a lower floor, or a Cerioni 1970 or DECODE Sforza key that fits. A key that
  fits would make this a known-key reading. A clear register copy in ASMi (Sforzesco, Potenze estere, Firenze)
  would also give a pair. I did not search for one.

## 2554: Piero Capponi to Lorenzo, 22 Jun 1486. Pass on the script figure, Readable flagged
- Image 30 is a full page of about 33 lines of continuous small sign cipher (9, 8, 3, z, w, q, x, =, pi) with no
  word division and heavy show-through.
- The script gives 18 px, but that figure is high because the signs join into runs: 717 components for about
  2300 signs. By eye at 3x, the body height is 8-10 px.
- Buildable rests on the glossed sisters, docs 6 and 13 in the same filza. The catalogue records a 22-sign key
  rebuilt from doc 13 that matches doc 6's gloss at 91.1%. I did not re-verify that today.
- The bare siblings 2555, 2556 and 2557 are in the same filza, so one key would open four letters.
- **The Vito key.** Vito, HistoCrypt 2025, publishes the "Cifera di Livorno ... di Piero Capponi" (ASF Misc.
  Repubblicana 11 fasc. 292). Vito dates it c. 1484-85 and calls it polyalphabetic. The PDF would not load:
  dspace.ut.ee refused the connection and then timed out. So its key table is unseen, and whether it fits doc 8
  is **unknown**. On present evidence this is not a known-key item.
- **Overlap risk.** Older vetting notes say Marco Vito is working on encrypted MAP letters of 1486-91 and has not
  published a list. Gate 0 should ask whether he covers filza XLIII.
- Paper record: https://dspace.ut.ee/items/5edf1ecc-b0ef-4d76-991d-521c22f9f30b
